claims.assertion: The trip drove 30.9 km against a recommended 20.6 km, a deviation of +10.3 km (+50%), which is far above the 1 km tolerance in RD-1.
The record splits the overrun into two off-route segments: 22:54–23:03 adding 5.71 km and 23:07–23:13 adding 4.73 km, 10.44 km in total, matching the +10.3 km deviation.

The driver's only justification for the reroute was 'Jam ahead', but the traffic record shows no incidents near the route and expressway speeds of 70+ km/h during the whole trip window, so there was no verified traffic reason under RD-4 for either segment (F14, F15 also show fair weather, 0.0 mm rain).

The driver's 22:50 message named only Upper Bukit Timah Road as one road to be taken, and my client's 'ok' at 22:51 was a short yes to that single named road, so at most one named road is agreed to; the second segment (23:07–23:13) drove Arcadia Road/Adam Road/Lornie Highway and did not drive Upper Bukit Timah Road at all, so no agreement covers it.

Even on the first segment, the named road was one link of a 7.16 km loop that the optimal route covers in 1.45 km and that strayed up to 1918 m from the route (F3); the named-road agreement cannot cover the later loop, and the driver's post-trip claim 'She agreed to my route' is a statement made after the trip, not the rider's consent before the segment.
The excess distance was billed at $14.54 (10.31 km × $1.4100/km) with no surge (1.0×), so the excess-distance fare measurable on this fare record is $14.54.

No part of the deviation is exempt under RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5, so the whole 10.31 km of excess distance is refundable as refund_partial of $14.54, and because there was no traffic reason a driver violation should be recorded (RD-2).
The driver has 1 upheld dispute in the last 90 days, so on this upheld deviation the repeat-deviation condition for flag_account is met.

The rider was not informed in the sense RD-5 requires for the whole route: the only notice given (22:50) was for a single road on the first segment and never covered the 23:07–23:13 loop, so the case also warrants the reminder and logging under RD-7.

The driver's statement 'She agreed to my route' (F11) will be used to argue broad consent, though it is post-trip and the system records (F3/F4) and the timed chat (F9) show the agreement reached only one named road.

The total is $57.56 (F7), over the $10 line, so under TH-1/TH-2 the system rules only at confidence ≥ 80% or escalates to human review; the rider's 2 disputes in 90 days (F16, none upheld) may be used against credibility, and the driver's 4.95 rating and 406 trips (F17) may be used to support the driver's credibility.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the actual distance was 30.9 km against a 20.6 km optimal route, so the deviation is +10.3 km, well over the 1 km tolerance — refund cannot be avoided in full; the honest driver-side ask is the excess distance fare only.

Segment 1 (22:54–23:03, +5.71 km) is covered by the rider's own consent: at 22:50, before the segment began, the driver asked 'Jam ahead, can go via Upper Bukit Timah Road?' and the rider replied 'ok' at 22:51, and UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD is among the roads this segment drove (F3).

Because the rider named and agreed to the named road UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD and the segment drove it, those 5.71 km are exempt from the refundable distance under RD-2's system detail, reducing the refundable deviation from 10.31 km to about 4.60 km.

Segment 2 (23:07–23:13, +4.73 km) has no rider message before it agreeing to any route: the chat record contains only two messages, both about Upper Bukit Timah Road, and no message covers ARCADIA ROAD, ADAM ROAD, LORNIE HIGHWAY, LORNIE ROAD, KHEAM HOCK ROAD, TREVOSE CRESCENT or MERRYN ROAD; the driver's later statement 'She agreed to my route' is a claim, not consent, and does not reach this segment.

On the fare record the excess distance billed is $14.54 (10.31 km × $1.4100/km), surge was 1.0×, and the only fare element a route deviation can touch is the distance fare — tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded.

The refundable amount should be computed on the 4.60 km not exempt under RD-3/RD-5 at this trip's rate of $1.4100/km, i.e. about $6.49, not the $14.54 the rider demands for 'the whole extra distance'.

The driver's documented record is strong (5.0 y account, 4.95 rating, 406 trips in 90 days, with no route deviation upheld against him), which is relevant to credibility and to whether any repeat-violation flag under RD-6 is warranted — the profile never decides the current case.
